subject: shortfin mako shark
title: The Fastest Shark Sometimes Ends Up Inside the Fishing Boat

scenes.text: Fishermen fear one shark for a strange reason: it might land in the boat.
The shortfin mako is the fastest shark known, with bursts estimated at up to about 45 miles an hour.
It uses that speed to chase down tuna and swordfish.
Point that speed upward, and a mako can leap about 20 feet into the air, the highest of any shark.
Hooked makos have crashed straight into fishing boats, like one off Maine in 2022.
So the boat isn't the safe side of the water.

description:
The shortfin mako is the fastest known shark and, according to Guinness World Records, the highest-leaping one, at about 6 meters (20 feet).
Burst speeds are often estimated at up to about 70 km/h (45 mph), though the fastest directly measured burst is lower; hooked makos have leapt into fishing boats, including one off Maine in August 2022.
Would you keep fishing after that?
first_comment: A shark that can land in your boat. Would you go deep-sea fishing after watching this?
